quick: 100 mg PO three times daily before meals
Use with caution; monitor liver enzymes
Symptom response, liver enzymes, prolactin if symptomatic
summary: Acotiamide is a prokinetic used for functional dyspepsia of the postprandial distress type, improving gastric accommodation and emptying. The usual dose is 100 mg three times daily before meals. It is approved in Japan and some other countries but is not FDA-approved; data below derive from manufacturer prescribing information and regulatory summaries.
indications: Functional dyspepsia (postprandial distress syndrome) - relief of postprandial fullness, upper abdominal bloating and early satiety
Improvement of impaired gastric accommodation and delayed gastric emptying associated with functional dyspepsia

dosage.n: Discontinue if no improvement after an adequate trial

admin: Take orally 100 mg three times daily before meals (approximately 30 minutes before eating)
Reassess the need for continued therapy if symptoms do not improve after an adequate trial
Use the lowest effective duration consistent with symptom control
moa: Acotiamide enhances gastrointestinal motility primarily by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, thereby increasing acetylcholine concentration at muscarinic synapses in the enteric nervous system. It also antagonizes inhibitory muscarinic M1/M2 autoreceptors, augmenting acetylcholine release. The net effect is improved gastric accommodation and accelerated gastric emptying, relieving postprandial distress symptoms.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to acotiamide or any component
relative: Mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction, perforation or hemorrhage
Severe hepatic or renal impairment (limited data)

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; avoid use during pregnancy unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Safety during breastfeeding has not been established; avoid use or discontinue nursing because excretion in human milk is not adequately characterized.
renal: Limited data in renal impairment; use with caution and monitor for adverse effects in patients with significant renal dysfunction.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; monitor liver function as transient hepatic enzyme elevations have been reported.

moderate: Anticholinergic agents - antagonize the prokinetic effect of acotiamide
Other cholinergic/cholinesterase-inhibiting drugs - potential additive cholinergic effects
minor: No clinically significant CYP-mediated interactions established
interactions.food: Administer before meals; food timing is part of the dosing instructions.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; moderate alcohol intake.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause transient elevations in hepatic transaminases and, rarely, prolactin.

monitoring: Symptom response (postprandial fullness, early satiety, bloating)
Liver function tests if symptoms suggest hepatic injury
Serum prolactin if galactorrhea or related symptoms occur
counsel: Take one tablet before each main meal, three times a day
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine or persistent fatigue
Let your doctor know if symptoms do not improve after the prescribed trial
Inform your doctor of all other medicines, especially those for stomach cramps or motion sickness
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless advised
pk: Symptomatic improvement over days to weeks
Store at controlled room temperature, protect from moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; approved in Japan (Acofide) and several other markets - data derive from manufacturer/regulatory prescribing information, not an FDA label
First-in-class agent specifically licensed for functional dyspepsia of the postprandial distress type
Works by acetylcholinesterase inhibition plus muscarinic autoreceptor antagonism to enhance gastric accommodation
Anticholinergic co-medication can negate its prokinetic effect
Monitor liver enzymes; reversible transaminase elevations have been reported
missed: Take the missed dose before the next meal when remembered. If it is nearly time for the next scheduled dose, skip it and continue the regular before-meal schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Cholinergic excess (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, salivation, bradycardia) is theoretically possible. Treat with general supportive measures and symptomatic care; atropine may counteract excessive cholinergic effects.
